questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Pristine nature area

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, the University of Warsaw had some good people to back us up and organizations such as ESN helped a lot too

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Support for getting into housing, course selection, recommended courses based on our interest, navigating the intranet (USOS) and support for slowly starting my master thesis.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Sokrates Guest House may be an old sovijet era building, but for the price it is an extremely attractive deal, especially if you plan on traveling around Poland and would like to spend your money on something other than rent.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Uber, Bolt and Freenow can save you in Warsaw when public transport is too slow. However mostly the public transport is excellent!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We booked a meeting after getting informed to do so on email and at the first day presentation.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Practical help, psychological safety support with regards to living abroad.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly successful. Unfortunately the faculty of Biology made 2 courses unavailable very late, and unnecessarily late too. One was changed to Polish and the other was a course that was cancelled due to "unforeseen circumstances" however this was well into the semester

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just show up in the intro week. it is so easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I'd say i was pleasantly surprised by the level of teaching. I found the botanical knowledge especially high and competent.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I took mainly field courses in Poland, and they compare well to danish standards.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
• Landscape-vegetation interactions in Northern Poland, 9 ECTS point
 • Ecology of Terrestrial Vertebrate Communities, 9 ECTS-point
 • Master level seminar (Specialization seminars for Biology), 2 ECTS-point
 • Diploma thesis preparation (Specialization workshop for 
Biology II), 9 ECTS-point
 • Agriculture, Food Production and Biodiversity, 4 ECTS-poin

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Field Mycology, 6 ECTS-point
Biodiversity Monitoring, 9 ECTS-poin

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are into botanics. Go for Landscape-vegetation interactions in Northern Poland AND Biodiversity Monitoring.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't get a great intro to this

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Travel the contry, see nature. Go to the mountains, go to the ancient forest (Bialoweiza).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Warsaw is a great city with something for everyone, i encourage you to explore the main streets, dont forget to cross the Vistula too!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people in the university world were very kind. And culture is not THAT different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go on fieldcourses! start in a lab group! Find a way to spend extended time with them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The lack of smiles on peoples faces threw me off a bit

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: History of Warsaw and Poland in general

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Become acquainted with locals, they know the systems´far better than you ever will.
Try the food! and the vodka lol
Remember to state your wishes and preferences, they go a long way to help you

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so no.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing and experiencing large functioning ecosystems.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trying to get some of the Polish people to speak english.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
